modern.text: An automatic watch has no battery, yet it must turn random wrist shakes into eight exact beats every second — twenty-eight thousand eight hundred beats an hour — and keep running for forty-two hours off the wrist.

Four subsystems share one 25.6 millimetre plate. On top sits the oscillating rotor and two reversing wheels. Beneath them sit the mainspring barrel, the geared going train, and the escapement coupled to the balance wheel.

Whenever your wrist tilts, gravity swings the heavy semicircular rotor. Two reversing click wheels catch both clockwise and counter-clockwise swings and mesh with the barrel ratchet to wind one way only through a one hundred and twenty to one reduction.

The winding train coils the alloy mainspring inside its toothed barrel. seven usable turns store forty-two hours of power. At full wind, a slipping bridle lets the outer coil slide safely against the smooth barrel wall at 7.2 newton millimetres so the rotor can never snap the spring.

Four geared stages connect the barrel to the escape wheel with a five thousand seven hundred and sixty to one ratio. The balance rate and the nine hundred and sixty to one train between center and escape wheels fix the center wheel at one turn an hour for the minute hand and the fourth wheel at one turn a minute for the second hand, while the six to one barrel stage paces the barrel at one turn every six hours.

Without an escapement, the mainspring would unwind in seconds. View A magnifies the fifteen-tooth escape wheel and ruby pallet fork. Every one hundred and twenty-five milliseconds, the balance impulse jewel enters the fork notch to unlock a ruby stone; a club tooth then slides across that stone to swing the fork, which kicks the balance jewel before another tooth drops and locks on the opposite stone, advancing the wheel twelve degrees per beat.

The poised balance wheel and breathing hairspring set the watch's rhythm. Even as barrel torque tapers, harmonic oscillation holds the period steady. Moving the regulator index shortens or lengthens the one hundred and eighty millimetre hairspring by just eighty-three microns to adjust daily rate by twenty seconds a day.
